prompt.context: Happy New Year's Eve! Thank you for coming in to help with this emergency deliverable. 5 pharma companies have developed 5 COVID vaccines and are now beginning to deliver them. Our client is the government of New York State and we will be providing ongoing support to the vaccine distribution until the end of the pandemic. The federal government is controlling distribution nationally and our client has been given extremely limited lots, as New York's Governor Drew Commo disputed the efficacy of the vaccines. The vaccine lots begin arriving to NYC in specially-outfitted refrigerated trucks tonight. You're here to help New York State make their final decision on how to distribute the initial vaccine lots that arrive this week in the manner that is best for the state. We have a call in 40 minutes with Governor Commo and his team. If approved, the distribution and administering of the available vaccines will begin tomorrow morning. If your recommendations are denied, we will lose the project and distribution will be delayed. Your recommendations will have life and death effects on New Yorkers.
prompt.question: How do we approach distribution of the vaccine lots arriving this week?

clarifying_info.q: What do you mean by best for the state?
clarifying_info.a: We want to save as many lives as possible and get our economy back up and running as soon as possible with the vaccines arriving this week. New York is facing a $10 billion shortfall on next year's budget. They have cut every extraneous item out of their budget that is viable. Governor Commo will reject any plan that does not cover the costs of the vaccines. A vaccinated person will immediately return to work in person.

clarifying_info.q: How does the vaccine work and how effective is it?
clarifying_info.a: The vaccines have varying degrees of effectiveness and are all administered by a series of or individual injections. An effectively vaccinated person cannot carry or spread the disease.

clarifying_info.q: How many doses or lots of vaccines do we have?
clarifying_info.a: We will address this later in the case. However, if you prefer, we can jump right into it.

clarifying_info.q: How many people can we inoculate?
clarifying_info.a: We will address this later in the case. That is what you are here to help figure out.

clarifying_info.q: How many people live in New York State?

clarifying_info.a: Recent studies show antibodies do not prevent reinfection or the spread of COVID and are ignored.

clarifying_info.q: How many people need to be inoculated?
clarifying_info.a: Current research indicates 90% of the US population needs to be inoculated before we can return to normal.

clarifying_info.q: What support can we expect from the Federal Government?
clarifying_info.a: Governor Commo believes asking for help is a sign of weakness and he will not directly admit his failure and ask the President for help as it would hurt his ego. We can expect no aid from the Federal Government.

exhibits.title: COVID Vaccines Details
exhibits.shows: A table listing each vaccine's name, manufacturing company, lot size (doses delivered), number of doses needed per inoculation series, vaccine effectiveness (%), and spoilage rate (%)

exhibits.title: COVID Vaccines Costs
exhibits.shows: A table listing each vaccine's cost per inoculation series, cost to administer per dose, total cost to transport the full lot, and arrival date in New York City

exhibits.title: Population Data
exhibits.shows: A table of New York State population segments by age range showing segment size, percentage classified as high-risk, percentage classified as low-risk, average taxable income, and the income effect (percentage increase to average taxable income) upon returning to in-person work after vaccination. Note: medium-risk individuals are those not classified as high- or low-risk; medium-risk people die or are hospitalized at a 5% rate if infected. The client cannot identify which individuals fall into which risk category. The effective tax rate for New York is 10%.

framework: 1. Vaccine Details: (a) Lot size per vaccine; (b) Doses needed per inoculation series (and booster reserve requirement); (c) Vaccine effectiveness %; (d) Spoilage %
2. Who Gets the Vaccine: (a) Population size and demographics (age, wealth, race, geography); (b) Risk level — frontline workers, healthcare heroes, high/medium/low risk segments

3. Paying for the Vaccines: (a) Vaccine costs — per series, transport, storage, administering; (b) Additional revenue sources — taxes from returning workers, subsidies, non-profit support, federal aid
4. Risks: (a) PR backlash; (b) Vaccine failure; (c) Adverse reactions; (d) Budget insolvency; (e) Anti-vaxxers; (f) Federal government intervention

questions.prompt: Question 2 (Exhibit 1): Given the vaccine details, calculate how many people can be effectively inoculated from the lots arriving this week.
questions.guidance: Candidate must: (1) subtract spoiled vaccines from each lot; (2) divide usable doses by doses-needed to find number of series completable; (3) multiply by effectiveness rate to find effectively inoculated people. Key insight: by federal decree the state must hold back enough doses to complete every started series — no gaming supply across a larger group. Note Apate and Dolos are NOT arriving this week (Jan 28 and Apr 1 respectively), so only Hermes, Mercurius, and Hamilkas arrive in time for the initial distribution decision.

math.setup: For each vaccine: (1) usable doses = lot_size * (1 - spoilage%); (2) completable series = usable doses / doses_needed; (3) effectively inoculated = completable series * effectiveness%
steps: Apate: 500k * 0.90 = 450k usable; 450k / 1 = 450k series; 450k * 90% = 405k effectively inoculated (not arriving this week)
Dolos: 2,000k * 0.90 = 1,800k usable; 1,800k / 1 = 1,800k series; 1,800k * 100% = 1,800k effectively inoculated (not arriving this week)
Total spoiled vaccines: 305k doses across all five; Total usable: 4,545k doses
Vaccines arriving this week (Hermes + Mercurius + Hamilkas): 190k + 300k + 225k = 715k people vaccinated; 171k + 285k + 225k = 681k effectively inoculated; 34k receive an ineffective vaccine
math.answer: 715k people vaccinated this week; 681k effectively inoculated (34k will receive an ineffective dose and can still contract/spread COVID)

questions.prompt: Question 3 (Exhibit 2): Calculate the total cost of the vaccines arriving this week and the all-in cost per person inoculated.
questions.guidance: Candidate must combine three cost components for each vaccine: (1) series cost = total doses / doses-needed * cost-per-series; (2) administration cost = usable (non-spoiled) doses * $4; (3) transport cost (flat per lot). Key note: cost-per-series is paid on ALL doses issued from manufacturer including spoiled ones. Only Hermes, Mercurius, Hamilkas arrive this week; total is ~$21.5m for 715k people (~$30/person), with only 681k effectively vaccinated.

math.setup: For each vaccine: series_cost = lot_size / doses_needed * cost_per_series; admin_cost = usable_doses * $4; total = series_cost + admin_cost + transport
steps: Apate (not this week): $5.5m total; Dolos (not this week): $14m total; combined all five = $41m
math.answer: $21.5m total cost for vaccines arriving this week; approximately $30 per person vaccinated (681k effectively)

questions.prompt: Question 4 (Exhibit 3): The state must cover vaccine costs from tax revenue generated when vaccinated workers return to in-person work. How many vaccines must be given to Segment C (age 36-59) to pay for the $21.5m in vaccines arriving this week, and how should the remaining doses be distributed?
questions.guidance: Candidate should quickly recognize that 681k / 19.5m = ~3.5% of NYS population — nowhere near the 90% herd immunity threshold. The key optimization is: use a minimum number of vaccines on working-age low-risk individuals (Segment C) to generate enough tax revenue to cover costs, then direct remaining doses to higher-risk elderly segments (D and E). Use Hamilkas (100% efficacy) for Segment C to maximize tax return certainty. Candidate should NOT try to calculate every cell in the exhibit — the important insight is identifying which segment pays for the vaccines and how many are needed.

math.setup: Tax revenue per Segment C vaccinated person = avg_income * income_effect * tax_rate; doses needed = total_cost / tax_revenue_per_person
steps: Tax revenue per Segment C person: $50k * 10% (income effect) * 10% (tax rate) = $500 per person per year
Hamilkas vaccines needed to pay for $21.5m: $21.5m / $500 = 43,000 Hamilkas vaccines to Segment C
Remaining this-week supply: 715k - 43k = 672k doses available for Segments D and E
Distribute remaining 672k (plus other Hamilkas/Mercurius/Hermes doses) to Segments D (age 60-70, 35% high-risk) and E (age >70, 60% high-risk), with preference for urban areas
math.answer: 43,000 Hamilkas vaccines to Segment C (working-age) to generate $21.5m in tax revenue; remaining ~672k doses to Segments D and E (elderly, highest-risk)

brainstorming.prompt: What are the implications of this distribution approach? (Economic, Health, and Moral dimensions)

categories.name: Economic
ideas: The more high-risk (elderly, non-working) people inoculated first, the slower the economic recovery as these individuals are less likely to return to productive in-person work
Giving vaccines to low-risk workers generates taxes that pay for the program, but this creates an explicit economic trade-off against protecting the most vulnerable
$10B budget shortfall means any plan that does not cover vaccine costs will be rejected by Governor Commo

categories.name: Health
ideas: Nine months of lockdown have caused incalculable damage to mental health across all age groups

We will be issuing vaccines with less than 100% effectiveness (Hermes at 90%, Mercurius at 95%) to high-risk citizens — 34k people will receive a non-effective dose and may have false confidence they are protected
305k doses are lost to spoilage; Mercurius has 0% spoilage — understanding how to match that standard could save tens of thousands of inoculations

categories.name: Moral
ideas: Asking the most vulnerable (elderly, high-risk) to continue isolation while lower-risk workers return to normal life raises significant ethical concerns
Politicians, bankers, and working-age individuals receiving vaccines before nursing home residents and people with disabilities would generate enormous public backlash
Antibodies from prior infection offer no protection; previously infected individuals must still be vaccinated, adding to the population count
Vaccine distribution decisions will visibly reflect societal value judgments about whose lives and whose economic contributions are prioritized

recommendation: Give 43,000 Hamilkas vaccines (100% efficacy) to Segment C (age 36-59, currently working) to generate $21.5m in tax revenue that covers the cost of all vaccines arriving this week

Distribute the remaining approximately 672,000 doses from Hermes, Mercurius, and Hamilkas to Segments D (age 60-70) and E (age >70) — the highest-risk populations — with priority given to those in urban areas where administration infrastructure is strongest
risks: We are giving vaccines to low-risk working individuals to fund the program, which delays protection for the elderly and highest-risk residents and risks their lives
Hermes (90%) and Mercurius (95%) are less than 100% effective; 34,000 recipients will not be effectively immunized yet may assume they are safe, potentially accelerating spread
We are prioritizing economic gain over front-line healthcare workers and the most vulnerable, which will face heavy PR resistance
Only ~3.5% of NYS population is vaccinated this week; 90% herd immunity threshold remains extremely far off
Distributing non-100%-effective vaccines to high-risk populations risks increasing the death toll if recipients act as though fully protected
next_steps: Immediately begin scheduling vaccine administration for the lots arriving Jan 1 (Hermes), Jan 3 (Mercurius), and Jan 5 (Hamilkas)
Develop a PR strategy that allows Governor Commo to present the distribution approach favorably while managing public expectations around efficacy and prioritization
Continue emphasizing safety measures (masking, distancing) across the full population given the minimal vaccination coverage achieved this week
Investigate how to reduce spoilage toward Mercurius's 0% standard to maximize effective doses from future lots
Plan distribution strategy for Apate (Jan 28) and Dolos (Apr 1) lots now that the cost-recovery model is established
